title: Trial economics experiment: credit sizing, expiry windows, and targeted upgrade nudges
creator: Jordan Liu
description:
Goal: Improve PLG conversion velocity and ARR per acquisition by tuning free trial credit allocation, expiry windows, and upgrade prompts. We want to find a configuration that maximizes paid conversion while minimizing credit spend and fraud risk.

Hypotheses:
1) Increasing initial free-credit quantum for new orgs from 50k tokens -> 150k tokens will increase 30-day paid conversion rate for mid-market cohorts by ~20% due to faster product exploration.
2) Shorter expiry windows (14 days) increase urgency and lead to higher short-term conversions but may reduce overall usage and perceived value; longer windows (60 days) increase engagement but delay upgrade signals.
3) A targeted upgrade prompt flow (in-app modal with prefilled enterprise contract link + sales SDR ping for >$1k MRR potential accounts) will materially lift conversion for accounts showing >80% credit consumption before expiry.

Experiment design (2x3 factorial with a separate nudging arm):
- Credit Size variants: Small=50k, Medium=100k, Large=150k tokens.
- Expiry variants: 14 days, 30 days, 60 days.
- Upgrade Prompt arm: Control (no upgrade nudge) vs Nudged (in-app + email + optional sales alert).
- Allocation: Randomized at org-level; stratified by region and initial signup source (self-serve vs partner).

Primary metrics:
- 30-day paid conversion rate (new orgs)
- 90-day paid conversion rate
- Time-to-first-paid-order (days)
- Net token usage per org before conversion
- Cost of free credits allocated per converted customer
- False-positive enterprise leads triggered (monitored via manual review)

Secondary metrics:
- Activation (first endpoint call within 24 hrs)
- Retention (starter week retention for usage intensity cohorts)
- Average revenue per converted org (ARPAC) at 90 days

Success criteria:
- Primary: A variant that yields >=15% relative uplift in 30-day conversion vs baseline with unit economics (credit cost per conversion) within budget assumptions.
- Secondary: Nudged arm increases conversion for high-usage orgs by >=10% without more than +20% increase in ops work for SDRs.

Instrumentation and tracking:
- Events: org.signup, credits.granted(amount, expiry), api.call(token_cost), upgrade_prompt.shown, upgrade_prompt.clicked, contract_initiated, sdr_alert.created.
- Dashboards: Growth dashboard (by variant) with conversion funnel and credit burn. Tracking dashboard link: https://grafana.internal.redwood/growth/pm-6831 (placeholder).
- Experiment id: EXP-2026-03-PM6831 (add to event payloads for cohort attribution).

Rollout plan:
1) Phase A (pilot): 2k new orgs over 10 days; deep analytics review and manual QA.
2) Phase B: Expand to 20k orgs for statistical power; run for 30 days.
3) Analysis and decision: 7-day analysis window + 10-day validation.

Risks & mitigations:
- Credit abuse/fraud: Limit per-org token burn velocity; apply device/email heuristics; partner with Security to flag anomalous patterns.
- Enterprise contract friction: Ensure enterprise contract link pre-fills minimal info and routes to sales queue; legal to review click-to-contract path prior to rollout.
- Instrumentation gaps: Add unit tests for event instrumentation (ENG-5998).

Dependencies (engineering & legal):
- ENG-5998: analytics instrumentation for credits and prompts
- ENG-6012: in-app modal & one-click contract plumbing
- ENG-6021: signup cohort segmentation service (region/source)
- LEG-128: enterprise contract quicklink + e-signature review

Notes on economics modeling:
- Baseline credit unit cost assumed: $0.001 per 1k tokens via avg compute uplift for hosted tier. Modeling spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/pm-6831-model (placeholder).

Deliverables:
- Experiment plan & success criteria (this doc)
- Instrumentation PRs and QA checklist
- A/B analysis notebook + postmortem with recommendations
- Updated onboarding copy and in-app prompts for the winning variant
